line: Crowley's account of Atu XIX: the Sun charged with a rose, Heru-ra-ha the Lord of the New Aeon, and the rose and cross.

sections.title: What Crowley says the card is
sections.line: The heraldic title and the figure he names. The planet Sun and the letter Resh come from the table only; no sentence in the chapter gives them.

quotes.quote: This card represents, in heraldic language, “the Sun, charged with a rose, on a mount vert
it represents Heru‐ra‐ha, the Lord of the New Aeon, in his manifestation to the race of men as the Sun spiritual, moral, and physical.

sections.title: What the card figures, in his words
sections.line: Crowley's reading of the rose and the Rose and Cross.

quotes.quote: The rose represents the flowering of the solar influence.
The card itself symbolizes this broadening of the idea of the Rose and Cross.

sections.title: Its path on the Tree
sections.line: The text gives no ends for this path. The table gives Key Scale path 30; the general rule is one letter to each of the twenty-two paths.
